name: libcamera
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  libcamera_version: "0.7.2"
  libcamera_rpi_version: "0.7.2+rpt20261009"
  # '+' must be percent-encoded for the GitHub release URL
  rpi_url_safe_version: ${{ libcamera_rpi_version | replace("+", "%2B") }}
  number_base: 0
  # rpi_fork sorts above upstream so a bare `libcamera` dep resolves to the
  # fork by default on aarch64 (where both variants exist); upstream stays
  # installable explicitly via `libcamera=*=*_upstream`. The offsets also clear
  # the previously published 0.7.1 builds (old upstream was 1+100=101), so each
  # new variant supersedes its predecessor.
  upstream_build_number: ${{ number_base + 100 }}
  rpi_build_number: ${{ number_base + 200 }}

recipe:
  name: libcamera
  version: ${{ libcamera_version }}

source:
  - if: variant == "upstream"
    then:
      # libcamera does not offer tarballs
      git: https://git.libcamera.org/libcamera/libcamera.git
      rev: v${{ libcamera_version }}
      patches:
        - memfd_symbols.patch
        # When cross compiling it is important to specify this to help find libevent
        - 0001-Specify-to-use-the-prefix-include-directory-to-help-.patch
        - 0002-conda-installed-paths.patch
        # conda-forge/libcamera-feedstock#38
        - 0003-measure-install-prefix-path-lengths-at-runtime.patch
    else:
      # raspberrypi/libcamera#251: upstream maintain ABI compatibility, so the
      # RPi-specific changes ship as a variant rather than a separate package.
      url: https://github.com/raspberrypi/libcamera/releases/download/v${{ rpi_url_safe_version }}/libcamera-${{ rpi_url_safe_version }}.tar.xz
      sha256: "509486fc6f8bce2804202ea20c902819358f898bf34f3167d7ceb2795fc01829"
      patches:
        - memfd_symbols.patch
        - 0001-Specify-to-use-the-prefix-include-directory-to-help-.patch
        - 0002-conda-installed-paths.patch
        # conda-forge/libcamera-feedstock#38
        - 0003-measure-install-prefix-path-lengths-at-runtime.patch

build:
  number: ${{ rpi_build_number if variant == "rpi_fork" else upstream_build_number }}
  skip:
    - not linux
    - variant == "rpi_fork" and not aarch64

outputs:
  - package:
      name: libcamera
    build:
      string: ${{ hash }}_${{ build_number }}_${{ variant }}
      script: build.sh
      dynamic_linking:
        # Relocate everything except the signed IPA modules: patching them
        # would invalidate their signatures (#19). build.sh sets their RPATH
        # and re-signs them instead.
        binary_relocation:
          - bin/**
          - libexec/**
          - lib/*.so*
          - lib/gstreamer-1.0/**
          - lib/python*/**
    requirements:
      # see https://git.libcamera.org/libcamera/libcamera.git/tree/meson.build?h=v0.5.1#n65
      run_exports:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('libcamera', upper_bound='x.x') }}
      build:
        - if: build_platform != target_platform
          then:
            - python
            - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
            - qt6-main
        - cmake
        - ninja
        - meson
        # Needed for some build processes???
        - ply
        - pyyaml
        - jinja2
        - pkgconf
        # re-sign IPA modules after setting their RPATH (see build.sh)
        - patchelf
        - openssl
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
      host:
        - libgl-devel
        - python
        - pybind11
        - jinja2
        - libudev
        - libudev1
        - gstreamer
        - libglib
        - glib
        - gst-plugins-base
        - libevent
        - libdrm
        - libtiff
        - qt6-main
        - libjpeg-turbo
        - yaml
        - libunwind
        - sdl2
        - openssl
        - libboost-devel
        - pyyaml
        - ply
        # Only the rpi/pisp pipeline uses libpisp, and libcamera only builds it on
        # aarch64; on linux-64 it would just be an unused (overdepending) pin.
        - if: aarch64
          then:
            - libpisp
      run:
        - python
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - libcamera
      - script:
          - cam -l
          # qcam -h would need a full X environment; just check it exists
          - which qcam
          - if: unix
            then: libcamerify -h
          # Verify env variables are set and point to existing directories
          - test -d "$LIBCAMERA_IPA_MODULE_PATH"
          - test -d "$LIBCAMERA_IPA_PROXY_PATH"
          - test -d "$LIBCAMERA_IPA_CONFIG_PATH"
          # #38: compile-time install paths must survive prefix replacement.
          # The global configuration.yaml lookup runs on every start (no camera
          # needed); with NUL-padded paths it opens the share/libcamera
          # directory and logs a parse error.
          - env -u LIBCAMERA_IPA_MODULE_PATH -u LIBCAMERA_IPA_PROXY_PATH -u LIBCAMERA_IPA_CONFIG_PATH cam -l > cam.log 2>&1 || true
          - if grep -aq "Failed to parse configuration file" cam.log; then cat cam.log; exit 1; fi
      - script:
          - python verify_ipa_signatures.py
          - python check_rpaths.py
        files:
          recipe:
            - verify_ipa_signatures.py
            - check_rpaths.py
        requirements:
          run:
            - openssl
            - patchelf
      - package_contents:
          files:
            - lib/libcamera.so
          include:
            - libcamera/libcamera/libcamera.h

  - package:
      name: libcamera-rpi
    build:
      number: ${{ number_base }}
      string: h${{ hash }}_${{ build_number }}_${{ variant }}
      skip:
        - variant == "upstream"
    requirements:
      run:
        # Can't pin exact because of the python build matrix; match the
        # version + build number + variant via the build-string glob instead.
        - libcamera ==${{ libcamera_version }} *_${{ rpi_build_number }}_${{ variant }}
    tests:
      # Metapackage: confirm it resolves the pin and co-installs the
      # matching libcamera build (the run dep lands in the test env).
      - script:
          - test -f $PREFIX/lib/libcamera.so
          - which cam

about:
  homepage: https://libcamera.org/index.html
  summary: An open source camera stack and framework for Linux, Android, and ChromeOS
  license: >
    LGPL-2.1-or-later
    AND BSD-2-Clause
    AND BSD-3-Clause
    AND MIT
    AND Apache-2.0
    AND CC0-1.0
    AND CC-BY-SA-4.0
    AND CC-BY-4.0
  license_file: LICENSES/
  documentation: https://libcamera.org/introduction.html
  repository: https://git.libcamera.org/libcamera/libcamera.git/

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - carlodri
